## About

I work on machine learning and decision systems. My background is in computational astrophysics; my current interests are learning, human judgement and how people work together.

The four chapters of this site run from a million stars to the person sitting next to you: science and its humanities held in one conversation. Chapter 01 is a complex adaptive system read from the outside in; the rest turns the same grammar of interaction and feedback on traffic, auctions, tools and teams.

## Background

### Computational astrophysics
Ph.D. Physics (2013–2018) · LSST Data Science Fellow

I began in computational astrophysics, studying stellar dynamics and binary black holes through numerical simulation and statistical modelling.

- Numerical simulations of globular clusters using N-body and Monte Carlo methods (3,240 MOCCA simulations across 662,772 globular clusters in 8,946 galaxies within 30 Mpc).
- [Globular cluster sandbox](https://domij.info/cluster/): a full-screen interactive model of the same physics — 1,650 stars evolving under gravitational relaxation and mass segregation, with colour, luminosity, radius and lifetime from MESA-based stellar-evolution relations, alongside the LISA strain and standard-siren localization for the dynamically formed binary black holes. The premise it was built to test: black holes formed dynamically inside a cluster are ejected into the halo, far from the local Galactic potential that perturbs every other timing clock, and so survive as unperturbed standard sirens — which, paired with an electromagnetic counterpart, make each one a multi-messenger probe of dark matter.
- Analysis of binary black hole evolution (17,883,760 inspiralling BBHs and 86,939 mergers), deriving a lower-bound local merger event rate of η ≃ 587 Gpc⁻³ yr⁻¹ and identifying 17 extragalactic standard sirens localized by LISA within ΔV ≤ 1 Mpc³ ([Dissertation essay chapter](https://domij.info/articles/research/astrophysics-bbh-dissertation.html) · [Full PDF](https://domij.info/pdfs/main.pdf)).
- LSST Data Science Fellowship: statistical modelling, image processing and reproducible research workflows.

### Decision systems
Applied ML & Decision Intelligence (2018–2024)

I then worked on machine learning for consumer products, marketplaces and advertising, where a model has to be useful within the constraints of a working system.

- Recommendation systems using behavioural and contextual signals from mobility data.
- Marketplace pricing, generative AI request workflows and information exchange between users.
- Advertising analytics, model evaluation and causal attribution; published architecture notes on real-time bidding and multi-agent control.

### Learning and human–AI collaboration
Independent projects & ventures (2018–present)

Building a company brought me closer to the people using the technology. It made me more attentive to what they need, and to the gap between a promising idea and something useful.

- Kin Domi, Inc.: AI and community projects concerned with older adults’ independence and access to technology.
- Open Learning Lab and baby-AI: open research into learning, and specifications for a household agent that runs on local hardware.
- Essays on learning, team coordination and human–AI collaboration in Domi’s Mind Waves and elsewhere.

## A question I keep returning to

What helps people make better decisions, learn well and work together?

## How I work

- **Working together**: Good work depends on more than individual ability. Shared context, trust, complementary skills and sensible incentives matter, as does room for people to exercise their own judgement.
- **Usefulness**: I judge technology by what it helps people do: understand a problem, make a choice, learn a skill or spend their time better. Technical elegance is valuable when it serves that purpose.
- **Testing the idea**: I try to make assumptions explicit, build something that can be tested and pay attention to the result. Revising an explanation is part of the work.

## Questions I am exploring

These are ongoing questions. The linked work distinguishes observations, proposals and research findings.

- **Collective Intelligence**: How do individual capabilities combine to produce collective outcomes?
- **Human–AI Collaboration**: How can intelligent systems support human judgement and agency?
- **Organisational Intelligence**: How do communication, coordination, trust, and incentives shape collaboration?
- **Complex Adaptive Systems**: How do interactions among individuals give rise to emergent social and organisational behaviour?
- **Decision Intelligence**: How can information, feedback, and experimentation improve decisions?
- **Human Potential**: How can technology make learning, opportunity, and meaningful participation more accessible?
- **AI and Society**: How might increasingly capable intelligence change the ways we work, cooperate, and live?

## Selected projects

Research notes, software and specifications at different stages of development. Design targets are not measured results; consult the linked work for evidence and status.

- **[Open Learning Lab](https://github.com/domijin/open-learning-lab)** ([Essay](https://domij.info/articles/github/open-learning-lab.html)): An open research ledger comparing approaches to learning with language models. The focus is on what learners retain and can apply independently, relative to the effort involved.
- **[baby-AI](https://github.com/domijin/baby-AI)** ([Essay](https://domij.info/articles/github/baby-ai.html)): Five subsystem specifications covering perception, speech recognition, memory, adaptation and evaluation. The design targets local hardware costing under $200, with signed evaluation records.
- **[Life Hack: iMessage AI Router](https://domij.info/beta/)**: An experiment in using iMessage to reach internet-connected agents when normal browsing is limited. It explores how a familiar, asynchronous interface can work with constrained connections.
- **[Kin Domi, Inc.](https://kindomi.net/)**: Work on AI companions, accessible interfaces and community activities in Palo Alto, informed by older adults’ experiences of technology, mobility and learning.
- **[Advertising decision systems](https://github.com/domijin/observations_in_advertising)** ([Essay](https://domij.info/articles/github/observations-in-advertising.html)): A four-stage ad-serving architecture — real-time ingestion and feature store, labelling and profile service, dynamic ad serving with in-session creative switching, and profile distillation for efficient candidate generation. Written up alongside notes on advertising economics and the growth trap.
- **[LibertyEarth & The Future Project](https://github.com/domijin/LibertyEarth)** ([Essay](https://domij.info/articles/github/libertyearth-and-future.html)): An evolving collection of proposals about social contracts, liquid democracy, local manufacturing and ways of turning ideas into practical experiments.
